name: pc.evidence-kms-profile.v1
authorityRules: Initial privileged installation pins the exact profile COSE digest, profile issuer, provider receipt signer, independent recovery authority, TLS destination/SPKI, Evidence workload and exact versioned KEK. Parsed claims, signatures or a static descriptor alone never admit key use.

PREPARE requests are exact original canonical JSON bytes containing operation=PREPARE, recipient, attemptId, objectIntent and challenge; SHA256 of those bytes is the immutable request identity. No keyId occurs in the pre-key object intent. Other requests contain operation, exchangeId, attemptId, recipient, originalRequestDigest, objectIntentDigest, keyId, keyUse and challenge. READ_ATTEMPT additionally binds readExchangeId and readRequestDigest to the exact original provider exchange being reconciled, including an uncertain unwrap. The installation digest resolves the exact independently installed profile.

Provider HTTPS responses use a canonical CBOR map of exactly nine integer keys: 0 profile payload, 1 profile COSE, 2 receipt payload, 3 receipt COSE, 4 wrapped-record payload, 5 wrapped-record COSE, 6 recovery-floor receipt payload, 7 recovery-floor COSE, 8 DEK. Values are byte strings; absent record/DEK is an empty byte string. Each signature uses its registered shared COSE family. Maximum response size is 66560 bytes (MAX_CBOR_BYTES + 1024); DEK is empty or exactly 32 bytes.

Non-exportable KEK and threshold escrow are required provider policies, not a production qualification inferred from this signed declaration or a local fixture. Only Evidence receives a bounded unwrapped DEK; never persist it in ordinary databases, logs or backups.
Current-encrypt, retained-decrypt, historical-record verification and recovery-floor evidence are separate admissions. No delivery, disclosure, hold removal or key destruction authority is conveyed.
